Positive association
As x increases, y tends to increase. The scatterplot rises from left to right.
Read the axes
Identify x and y. Look at the overall point cloud, not just one pair.
Exact example
Points one three, two five, three seven, four nine, five eleven follow y equals two x plus one.
Noisy trends
Positive association does not require every next y to be larger. Look for an overall upward tendency.
Best-fit line
An upward line has positive slope. Between two five and six thirteen, slope is two.
Prediction
For y equals two x plus three, at x seven the prediction is seventeen.
Correlation
Positive r indicates positive linear direction. A value close to positive one indicates a strong positive pattern.
Outliers
A point far from the upward pattern can weaken the correlation.
Causation
Association does not prove that one variable causes the other.
Residual
Residual is observed minus predicted. Sixteen minus fourteen equals two.
Exam strategy
Read direction, strength, slope and units. Avoid unjustified causal claims.
